contract_and_source_assessment.result: B changes the desired_velocity that the Host solver receives to zero as an opt-in test configuration. Core task/route/command storage and production policy code remain unchanged, but the solver input demand is explicitly different. This is not evidence that the Host failed to fulfil an unchanged command, not terrain authority and not natural weapon integration.

The same fixed warmup and identity-order predicate in Hosted A/B and Original requires a real final-warmup move answer with finite motion above one and an actually supplied finite positive desired_velocity. None-terrain inputs remain valid. Missing, nonnumeric, nonfinite or nonpositive demands are ineligible; absence is an honest prelaunch UNREACHED.

Only within the one prepare-to-run engine frame, for the watched target move callback with a finite positive incoming demand, B makes one shallow copy changing only desired_velocity to zero. Nested tables and all other values are reused unchanged. The received Engine table is not mutated. There is one delegation per actual callback to the same Movers; the answer, pose, getters, solver and normal Core result application are not edited. Incoming demand and substituted zero are recorded; transformed/delegated counts remain distinct.

New warmup observation uses type/finiteness/sign checks and stores the actual demand, not a computed replacement. The only transformation is the declared zero demand in the bounded window. Delegation credit increments after the Host returns. Missing/invalid demand or no actual window step creates no change and no credit. No additional random draws, second store or movement computation was added.

A retains per-target NeedUpdated, test and moving16. Hosted B requires an actual transformed delegation, post-transform target offer/answer, contract/mirror coherence and physical signature different from authentic A. B may legitimately broadphase-skip the moving read; that does not weaken A. Original requires no hosted entity/candidate/scan/pose questions. Its optional Lua signature is not authority by itself: Root runner binds actual matched A and enforces changed output and input joins.

Seven added tests use the real driver with sociable Engine/Host collaborators. They check positive selection, skipped ineligible values, terrain-less support, unchanged A, only-one-field copy and one delegation, non-target/warmup preservation, missing/invalid/no-window inputs, strict A versus allowed B broadphase skip, absent offer/control and unchanged result rejection, plus Original behavior. Scripted ray results depend on the demand received by the stand-in; they are not evidence that real solver output changes a retail query.
